questions.question: A student burns a small piece of ethanol under a copper can of water. Which statement best describes how energy is transferred to the water?
options: Chemical energy in the ethanol is destroyed and recreated inside the water.
The burning fuel transfers energy to the water and can by heating the surroundings.
The fuel absorbs thermal energy from the water, which raises the temperature of the water.
Chemical energy from the surroundings is converted directly to mechanical work inside the water.

questions.question: To compare the energy content of two different liquid fuels, a student heats a fixed volume of water in a boiling tube using each fuel. What observation would indicate which fuel transfers more energy per gram?
options: The fuel that produces the smallest temperature rise in the water per gram burned.
The fuel that takes the longest time to extinguish after the flame is covered.
The fuel that produces the largest temperature rise in the water per gram burned.
The fuel that leaves the most soot on the bottom of the boiling tube.

questions.question: A student wants to fairly compare the energy transferred by burning methanol and ethanol using a water calorimeter. Why must the student ensure that the mass of fuel burned is identical in both tests?
options: To ensure that both fuels have the exact same chemical structure during the reaction.
Because different masses of fuel would release different amounts of energy, making the temperature change comparison invalid.
To guarantee that the volume of water in the boiling tube does not evaporate during heating.
Because the mass of the fuel determines the boiling point of the water being heated.

questions.question: In an experiment comparing three fuels, a student uses 20 ml of water starting at 20 degrees Celsius for Fuel A, 40 ml of water starting at 20 degrees Celsius for Fuel B, and 20 ml of water starting at 30 degrees Celsius for Fuel C. Why is this experimental setup invalid?
options: The volume of water must be kept constant, but the starting water temperature has no effect on the final temperature rise.
Both the starting temperature and the volume of water must be kept the same to ensure the energy transferred causes a comparable temperature change.
The starting temperature of the water must be higher than the boiling point of the fuel for the test to work.
Only the room temperature needs to be controlled; the water volume and starting temperature are independent variables.

questions.question: A liquid substance is cooled from 100 degrees Celsius to 20 degrees Celsius, and its temperature is plotted over time. A flat, horizontal line (plateau) is observed on the graph between minutes 5 and 10. What is happening during this time interval?
options: The substance is rapidly heating up due to an endothermic process.
The substance is undergoing a state change, such as freezing, where temperature remains constant.
The substance is completely solid and its molecules have stopped moving.
The thermometer has failed and is no longer registering temperature changes.

questions.question: While stearic acid cools and changes from a liquid to a solid in a boiling tube, what is happening to the energy of the system?
options: The stearic acid is absorbing energy from the surroundings to break chemical bonds.
The stearic acid is transferring energy into the surroundings by heating as it freezes.
Energy is being created inside the stearic acid, causing it to become a solid.
No energy transfer occurs because the temperature of the substance remains constant during the state change.

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon is added to hydrochloric acid in a polystyrene cup, the temperature of the solution rises from 21 degrees Celsius to 35 degrees Celsius. How should this reaction be classified?
options: Endothermic, because energy is absorbed from the surroundings to break bonds.
Exothermic, because it causes an increase in the temperature of the surroundings.
Endothermic, because the chemical products have more energy than the reactants.
Exothermic, because energy is destroyed during the reaction.

questions.question: A student dissolves ammonium nitrate in water. The temperature of the mixture drops from 22 degrees Celsius to 14 degrees Celsius. Which statement correctly explains this observation?
options: It is an endothermic reaction because energy is taken in, causing a decrease in the temperature of the surroundings.
It is an exothermic reaction because the surroundings lose thermal energy to the reactants.
It is a physical change that is neither endothermic nor exothermic because no gas was produced.
It is an endothermic reaction because energy is released, cooling down the water molecules.

questions.question: During a combustion reaction in a fireplace, how is energy transferred between the chemical system and the room?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings into the chemical reactants.
Energy is transferred from the chemical reactants to the surroundings.
Energy is created within the surroundings without any transfer from the reactants.
Energy is transferred from the products to the reactants, keeping the surroundings cool.

questions.question: In a thermal decomposition reaction, copper carbonate is heated. Which statement describes the energy transfer in this endothermic process?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the products.
Energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings.
The chemical products transfer energy back to the bunsen burner flame.
No energy transfer occurs because the temperature of the system decreases.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of phase changes all require energy to be transferred into the substance from the surroundings, making them endothermic?
options: Freezing, condensing, and boiling
Melting, evaporation, and boiling
Melting, freezing, and condensing
Evaporation, condensing, and freezing

questions.question: When water vapour in the air touches a cold windowpane, it turns into liquid water droplets. Which statement correctly describes this process?
options: This is condensing, which is an endothermic process that absorbs energy from the window.
This is freezing, which is an endothermic process that releases energy to the window.
This is condensing, which is an exothermic process that transfers energy to the surroundings.
This is evaporation, which is an exothermic process that cools the windowpane.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the current mix of electricity generation in the UK?
options: Over half of the electricity is generated from renewable sources like the Sun, wind, and falling water.
Coal-fired power stations still generate more than 75% of the UK's electricity.
Nuclear power is the sole source of electricity, with solar and wind contributing less than 5%.
Over 90% of electricity is generated by burning imported wood pellets in thermal power stations.

questions.question: In many non-renewable thermal power stations across the UK, what is the primary method used to produce the high-pressure steam needed for electricity generation?
options: Splitting water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen gases using solar energy.
Burning fossil fuels like natural gas and oil to heat water.
Using geothermal heat from deep volcanic rocks to boil groundwater.
Burning coal in large open furnaces to directly heat the turbines.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the mechanical steps that occur inside a steam-driven power station to generate electricity?
options: Burning gas directly spins the generator, which pushes steam through the turbines.
Moving steam pushes turbines, which drive electric generators to produce electricity.
Electric generators create steam, which then spins the turbines to burn the fuel.
Turbines heat the water to make steam, which spins the electric generator.

questions.question: How has the use of fossil fuels in UK power stations changed in recent years?
options: Coal has completely replaced natural gas and oil as the main source of power.
Natural gas and oil are still used, but coal is no longer used in UK power stations.
No fossil fuels of any kind are permitted to be burned for electricity in the UK.
Coal and oil are widely used, while natural gas has been completely banned.

questions.question: A local community is debating whether to replace a natural gas power plant with a biomass plant that burns wood and waste. What environmental factor must they consider regarding both options?
options: Neither natural gas nor wood produces any greenhouse gases or pollutants when burned.
Only natural gas produces pollutants, while burning wood and waste is completely emissions-free.
Both natural gas and biomass (wood and waste) are fuels that produce greenhouse gases and pollutants when burned.
Burning waste produces only oxygen and water vapor, whereas natural gas produces sulfur dioxide.

questions.question: Why are energy resources such as wind, solar, and hydroelectric classified as 'renewable'?
options: They do not require any turbines or generators to produce electricity.
They can be recycled in a laboratory after they have been used once.
They will not run out because they are replenished more quickly than we use them up.
They release energy through highly controlled nuclear fusion reactions.

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only energy sources that can be burned to produce moving steam to spin a turbine?
options: Wind, solar, and falling water
Biomass, oil, and gas
Solar panels, geothermal, and wind
Uranium, wind, and falling water

questions.question: How does electricity generation using solar panels differ fundamentally from generation using wind turbines or fossil-fuel power stations?
options: Solar panels require steam to be created before they can function.
Solar panels produce electricity directly without using electric generators.
Solar panels must use an electric generator spun by light beams.
Solar panels are highly polluting because they must burn silicon to work.

questions.question: A student burns a small piece of ethanol under a beaker of water. They observe that the temperature of the water increases. Which statement best explains this energy transfer?
options: Chemical energy stored in the fuel is destroyed, creating thermal energy in the water.
Burning the fuel transfers energy by heating to its surroundings, which includes the water.
Energy is transferred from the cold water into the burning fuel to make it burn faster.
The fuel absorbs heat from the air, which is then concentrated into the water.

questions.question: To compare the energy released by burning ethanol versus burning propanol, a student heats a fixed volume of water in a boiling tube with each fuel. What is the primary purpose of using a boiling tube of water in this experiment?
options: To act as a reservoir that absorbs and measures the energy transferred by each fuel.
To prevent the fuel from evaporating into the air before it can be ignited.
To speed up the combustion reaction of the fuels so they burn completely.
To keep the fuel at a constant temperature throughout the burning process.

questions.question: A student wants to compare the energy output of two different liquid fuels. They set up two identical boiling tubes with water. Why must they ensure that the mass of fuel actually burned is identical in both tests?
options: To ensure that both fuels reach their boiling points at the exact same time.
Because a larger mass of the same fuel would transfer more energy, making the comparison unfair.
To guarantee that the chemical composition of the fuels does not change during combustion.
Because the mass of the fuel directly determines the volume of water that can fit in the tube.

questions.question: In an experiment comparing the energy content of food fuels, why is it essential to use the exact same starting temperature and volume of water in the boiling tube for every test?
options: To ensure the water reaches its boiling point of 100°C in every single test.
Different starting temperatures and volumes would affect the temperature rise, preventing a fair comparison of energy transferred.
To make sure that the mass of the fuel consumed remains completely constant.
Because water changes its chemical composition if heated from different initial temperatures.

questions.question: A liquid substance is left to cool, and its temperature is recorded over time. The resulting graph shows a sloping line downwards, then a flat horizontal section, followed by another downward slope. What is happening during the flat horizontal section?
options: The substance is warming up rapidly due to an endothermic process.
The substance is changing state, and the temperature remains constant during this time.
The thermometer has stopped working because the substance has become too cold.
The substance is cooling at its fastest rate because there is no energy transfer.

questions.question: When gaseous water vapor cools and condenses into liquid water on a cold windowpane, what is happening to the energy of the system?
options: Energy is absorbed by the water vapor from the cold windowpane.
Energy is transferred from the water vapor to the surroundings by heating.
No energy is transferred because condensation is a purely physical shape change.
Energy is created within the water droplets to help them stick to the glass.

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon is added to hydrochloric acid in a polystyrene cup, the temperature reading on the thermometer increases from 21°C to 35°C. How should this reaction be classified and why?
options: Endothermic, because the system is absorbing heat from the thermometer.
Exothermic, because energy is transferred to the surroundings, raising the temperature.
Endothermic, because chemical bonds are being broken which always releases coldness.
Exothermic, because the mass of the solution decreases during the reaction.

questions.question: A student dissolves ammonium nitrate in water and notices that the beaker feels extremely cold to the touch, with the thermometer showing a drop of 12°C. What does this temperature decrease indicate?
options: The reaction is endothermic because it has transferred energy from the surroundings.
The reaction is exothermic because it has released cold energy into the surroundings.
The reaction is endothermic because it has destroyed thermal energy inside the beaker.
The reaction is exothermic because the temperature of the reactants has increased.

questions.question: During a neutralisation reaction between sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid, energy is transferred. Which of the following correctly describes the energy flow in this exothermic reaction?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings into the chemical products.
Energy is transferred from the chemical reactants to the surroundings.
Energy is created out of nothing and stored entirely within the chemical bonds.
Energy is transferred from the container walls into the reacting mixture.

questions.question: Photosynthesis is a chemical process where green plants convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen using light. Which statement correctly describes the energetics of this process?
options: It is endothermic because energy is transferred from the surroundings (sunlight) to the products.
It is exothermic because it releases oxygen which contains high thermal energy.
It is endothermic because energy is transferred from the plant's roots to the soil.
It is exothermic because glucose stores less energy than the carbon dioxide and water.

questions.question: Why must you continuously heat a beaker of liquid water on a Bunsen burner to keep it boiling?
options: Because boiling is an exothermic process that requires a spark to keep it going.
Because boiling is an endothermic process that requires a continuous transfer of energy from the surroundings to break intermolecular forces.
Because water absorbs cold from the air and needs constant neutralisation by the flame.
Because the steam produced cools down the remaining liquid, which must be reheated.

questions.question: When liquid water is placed in a freezer, it eventually turns into ice. Which statement correctly describes the thermal energy transfer during this freezing process?
options: Ice actively absorbs coldness from the freezer, making freezing an endothermic process.
Freezing is an exothermic process because the water must transfer energy to its surroundings to form solid bonds.
Freezing is endothermic because energy must be added to the water to make its molecules stop moving.
No energy is transferred because freezing only changes the shape of the water molecules.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the current sources used to generate the majority of electricity in the UK?
options: Coal-fired power stations still produce over 80% of the UK's electricity.
Over half of the electricity in the UK is generated from renewable sources like the Sun, wind, and falling water.
Nuclear power is the sole source of over 95% of the UK's electrical energy.
The UK imports all of its electricity from European solar farms.

questions.question: In many UK thermal power stations, how is the water heated to produce the high-pressure steam required for electricity generation?
options: By utilizing geothermal heat directly from deep volcanic vents.
By burning fossil fuels like natural gas and oil to release thermal energy.
By using electricity from the grid to power large immersion heaters.
By mixing acids and alkalis in massive exothermic neutralization tanks.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of energy transfers and mechanical events in a typical fossil-fuel-burning power station?
options: Burning fuel heats steam -> steam directly powers the generator -> generator spins the turbine.
Burning fuel heats water to make steam -> moving steam pushes turbines -> turbines drive generators to produce electricity.
Steam is condensed into water -> water spins the generator -> generator heats the turbine.
Electricity spins the generator -> generator drives the turbine -> turbine produces steam.

questions.question: A student is analyzing the types of fossil fuels currently used to generate electricity in UK power stations. Which of the following statements correctly summarizes current practice?
options: Coal remains the primary fossil fuel, while natural gas has been completely banned.
Natural gas and oil are still used in power stations, but coal is no longer used.
Coal and oil are used extensively, but natural gas is only used for domestic cooking.
All fossil fuels, including natural gas, oil, and coal, have been completely phased out of UK power stations.

questions.question: Some power stations burn wood pellets (biomass) or municipal waste instead of coal. Why must we still be concerned about the atmospheric impact of burning these fuels?
options: Burning wood and waste does not produce any heat, only smoke.
Like natural gas and oil, burning waste and wood still produces greenhouse gases and pollutants.
Wood and waste release large amounts of helium, which depletes the ozone layer.
They consume all the oxygen in the atmosphere, leaving none for respiration.

questions.question: Why are solar energy, wind energy, and hydroelectric power classified as "renewable" energy resources?
options: Because they can be recycled in a laboratory after they have been used to make electricity.
Because they are replenished more quickly than we use them up, meaning they will not run out.
Because they do not require any turbines or generators to produce electricity.
Because they release carbon dioxide which helps plants grow faster, renewing the forests.

questions.question: How can thermal power stations that burn biomass, oil, or gas be adapted to use the same basic turbine and generator setup?
options: They cannot; each fuel requires a completely different type of turbine that does not use steam.
The heat from burning any of these fuels is used to boil water, creating moving steam that spins the turbine.
The fuel itself is sprayed directly onto the turbine blades to make them spin by chemical pressure.
These fuels are mixed with water to make a thick liquid that is pumped through the turbine.

questions.question: Most utility-scale electricity generation methods rely on spinning generators. How do solar photovoltaic panels differ from these traditional methods?
options: Solar panels use tiny internal steam turbines powered by light.
Solar panels produce electricity directly from sunlight without using an electric generator.
Solar panels must be connected to wind turbines to function.
Solar panels use chemical combustion of silicon to spin miniature internal motors.

questions.question: When a fuel like ethanol is burned in a spirit burner, how is energy transferred to the air and any container held above it?
options: By heating the surroundings as thermal energy is released
By transferring electrical work to the air molecules
By absorbing thermal energy from the container to break chemical bonds
By cooling the surrounding air through endothermic work

questions.question: A student wants to compare the energy released by burning equal volumes of two liquid fuels. How can they practically measure and compare this energy transfer in a school laboratory?
options: By measuring the volume of gas produced in a gas syringe
By using the fuels to heat water in a boiling tube and measuring the temperature change
By weighing the ash remaining after combustion is complete
By measuring the brightness of the flame using a light sensor

questions.question: In an experiment comparing the energy output of ethanol and propanol, why must the teacher ensure that exactly 1.0 g of each fuel is combusted during the heating process?
options: To ensure the flame temperature of both fuels is identical
To ensure a fair comparison of the energy transferred per unit mass of fuel
To keep the volume of water in the boiling tube constant
To prevent the fuels from evaporating before they are lit

questions.question: When comparing the energy transferred by different fuels, a student uses 20 cm³ of water at 20 °C for the first fuel. Why must they use 20 cm³ of water at 20 °C for the second fuel?
options: To ensure the chemical reactions in the water occur at the same rate
To ensure that any change in water temperature reflects only the energy transferred by the fuel
To prevent the water from boiling and evaporating too quickly
To match the mass of the fuel being burned in the spirit burner

questions.question: When analyzing a cooling curve graph of a liquid substance as it turns into a solid, what feature on the graph indicates that a state change is actively occurring?
options: A steep, constant downward slope
A flat, horizontal plateau where the temperature remains constant
An exponential increase in temperature over time
A sudden vertical drop to absolute zero

questions.question: As a sample of gaseous substance cools down and transitions into a liquid, what is happening to the energy of the substance and its surroundings?
options: The substance absorbs energy from the surroundings while it condenses
The substance transfers energy into the surroundings by heating as it condenses
The temperature of the substance increases as it releases energy
There is no net energy transfer because the state change is physical, not chemical

questions.question: A student mixes two solutions in a polystyrene cup and measures the temperature of the mixture. If the temperature increases from 21 °C to 28 °C, what does this indicate about the reaction?
options: The reaction is endothermic and absorbs energy from the cup
The reaction is exothermic and causes an increase in the temperature of the surroundings
The reaction is physical and does not involve any energy transfer
The reaction has destroyed energy, causing the surroundings to cool down

questions.question: When ammonium chloride dissolves in water, the temperature of the solution drops from 20 °C to 14 °C. How should this chemical reaction be classified?
options: Exothermic, because energy is released to the surroundings
Endothermic, because it causes a decrease in the temperature of the surroundings
Exothermic, because the chemical bonds in the products are weaker
Endothermic, because the temperature of the reactants has increased

questions.question: During an exothermic reaction, what is the net direction of energy transfer between the reacting chemicals and their environment?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings into the chemical products
Energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings
Energy is created within the surroundings without affecting the reactants
Energy is transferred from the products to the reactants

questions.question: How is energy transferred during an endothermic reaction such as thermal decomposition?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the products
Energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings
Energy is transferred from the products to the surroundings
Energy is destroyed as reactants turn into products

questions.question: Why are physical processes like melting, evaporation, and boiling classified as endothermic changes of state?
options: They release thermal energy to the surroundings, cooling the substance down
They require energy to be transferred into the substance from the surroundings
They occur spontaneously without any exchange of energy
They cause the temperature of the surroundings to rise significantly

questions.question: When steam condenses onto a cold window pane, what type of energy change occurs?
options: An endothermic change, because the steam absorbs heat from the glass
An exothermic change, because energy is transferred to the surroundings during condensing
An endothermic change, because the temperature of the glass decreases
No energy change occurs because condensation is a purely chemical process

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the current state of electricity generation sources in the United Kingdom?
options: Over half of the electricity is generated from the Sun, wind, and falling water
Over 90% of electricity is generated by burning coal in large power stations
The UK relies entirely on nuclear power to generate its electricity
Electricity is primarily generated using geothermal energy from active volcanoes

questions.question: In many modern UK thermal power stations, which fuels are burned to heat water and convert it into high-pressure steam?
options: Coal and biomass only
Natural gas and oil
Uranium and wood pellets
Hydrogen and wind power

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes how electricity is generated in a gas-fired power station?
options: Burning gas spins the generator directly, which heats water into steam
Moving steam pushes turbines, which drive electric generators to produce electricity
Steam directly creates an electric current in the boiler which flows to the grid
Turbines burn the fuel directly to release electrons into the water

questions.question: Which of the following fossil fuels is no longer used to generate electricity in UK power stations?
options: Natural gas
Oil
Coal
Biogas

questions.question: Burning which group of fuels releases greenhouse gases and pollutants into the atmosphere?
options: Natural gas, oil, waste, and wood
Wind, solar, and falling water
Geothermal, nuclear, and tidal energy
Hydrogen gas and pure oxygen

questions.question: Why are energy resources like wind and solar described as renewable?
options: They produce no waste materials when they are manufactured
They are replenished more quickly than we use them up and will not run out
They can be burned repeatedly without being consumed
They generate electricity without needing to spin any machinery

questions.question: How can biomass, oil, or gas be used to spin a turbine in a power station?
options: By burning them to produce moving steam that pushes the turbine blades
By dropping them from a height onto the turbine blades
By using them to lubricate the generator coils so they spin faster
By reacting them with acids to create high-pressure hydrogen gas

questions.question: How does electricity generation using solar panels differ from generation using wind turbines?
options: Solar panels require a steam cycle to generate a current
Solar panels produce electricity without using electric generators
Solar panels require spinning coils of wire inside magnetic fields
Solar panels must burn silicon fuel to release electricity

questions.question: A student burns a small piece of ethanol under a beaker of water. Which statement best explains how the energy change is detected in this setup?
options: The fuel gains energy from the water, lowering the water's temperature.
Burning the fuel transfers energy by heating the surroundings, which increases the temperature of the water.
The combustion reaction absorbs thermal energy from the air, making the beaker cold.
The chemical bonds in the water break, releasing energy that heats the ethanol.

questions.question: To compare the energy output of two different liquid fuels, a student heats water in a boiling tube using a spirit burner. Why is this method effective for comparing energy transfers?
options: Water has a very low boiling point, so it boils instantly to show the maximum energy.
The rise in water temperature serves as an indicator of the relative amount of energy transferred by each fuel.
The boiling tube prevents any energy from escaping to the air, ensuring 100% efficiency.
It allows the student to measure the chemical mass of the heat directly rather than temperature.

questions.question: In an experiment to compare the energy released by ethanol and propanol, a student wants to ensure a fair comparison of the fuels' properties. Why must the mass of each fuel burned during the test be kept identical?
options: Because different fuels must transfer the exact same total energy to the water.
To ensure that the energy transferred per unit mass can be compared directly.
Because heavier fuels always have a lower boiling point than lighter fuels.
To keep the volume of water in the boiling tube from evaporating.

questions.question: When comparing the energy transferred by different fuels using a water-heating setup, which set of water variables must be kept constant to ensure the comparison is valid?
options: The initial temperature of the water and the volume of water used.
The final boiling temperature of the water and the mass of the boiling tube.
The volume of water and the duration the water is allowed to boil.
The depth of the thermometer in the water and the chemical purity of the fuel.

questions.question: A scientist cools a sample of liquid stearic acid and records its temperature over time. On the resulting cooling curve, a flat, horizontal section (plateau) is observed. What does this plateau represent?
options: The substance is heating up rapidly due to an endothermic process.
A change of state is occurring, during which the temperature remains constant.
The substance has completely evaporated and no longer has a measurable temperature.
The thermometer has reached its minimum physical limit and cannot measure lower temperatures.

questions.question: As a hot gas cools down in a closed container, it eventually turns into a liquid. Which of the following describes the energy transfer and state change occurring during this process?
options: The substance transfers energy into the surroundings by heating and condenses.
The substance absorbs energy from the surroundings and freezes.
The substance transfers energy into the surroundings and evaporates.
The substance absorbs energy from the surroundings and condenses.

questions.question: A beaker of hot water is left on a laboratory bench. Over 30 minutes, the temperature of the water decreases from 80 °C to 25 °C. What is happening to the energy of the water during this time?
options: Energy is being created inside the water, causing its particles to slow down.
Energy is absorbed from the colder surroundings, causing the water temperature to drop.
Energy is released to the surroundings as the water cools, observed as a decrease in its temperature.
Energy is converted into mass, making the water heavier as it cools.

questions.question: In a school lab, a student mixes two solutions in a polystyrene cup. The temperature of the mixture increases from 21 °C to 29 °C. How should this chemical reaction be classified?
options: Endothermic, because energy is absorbed by the reactants from the thermometer.
Exothermic, because it causes an increase in the temperature of the surroundings.
Endothermic, because the chemical bonds in the products contain more energy than the reactants.
Exothermic, because the system has absorbed thermal energy from the air.

questions.question: When ammonium nitrate dissolves in water, the temperature of the solution drops from 20 °C to 12 °C. What type of reaction is this, and why?
options: Exothermic, because energy is released, lowering the temperature of the surroundings.
Endothermic, because it causes a decrease in the temperature of the surroundings.
Exothermic, because the water molecules gain kinetic energy.
Endothermic, because the temperature of the surroundings increases to balance the system.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the energy transfer in an exothermic chemical reaction?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the reactants.
Energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings.
Energy is created within the products without any transfer.
Energy is destroyed to lower the temperature of the products.

questions.question: During an endothermic reaction, how is energy exchanged between the system and its environment?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the products.
Energy is transferred from the products to the surroundings.
Energy is released as light, causing the surroundings to warm up.
No energy is exchanged because the reaction occurs instantly.

questions.question: When solid ice is heated, it turns into liquid water, and with further heating, it becomes water vapor. What is the role of heating in these state changes?
options: Heating transfers energy out of the substance, causing its bonds to strengthen.
Heating transfers energy into the substance, which can cause it to melt, evaporate, or boil.
Heating destroys the molecules, converting them into pure thermal energy.
Heating keeps the temperature of the substance constant without changing its physical state.

questions.question: Why are melting, evaporation, and boiling classified as endothermic processes?
options: They release energy to the surroundings, causing a temperature rise.
They require energy to be transferred into the substance from the surroundings.
They decrease the overall internal energy of the substance.
They occur only when the surroundings are at absolute zero.

questions.question: What thermodynamic classification do condensing and freezing fall under, and why?
options: Endothermic, because they require the substance to absorb heat from the surroundings.
Exothermic, because energy is released to the surroundings during these processes.
Endothermic, because the temperature of the substance must increase to change state.
Exothermic, because they destroy thermal energy to make the particles move faster.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the modern generation of electricity in the United Kingdom?
options: Over half of the electricity is generated from the Sun, wind, and falling water.
Almost all electricity is generated by burning coal in large thermal power stations.
No electricity is generated from renewable sources like wind or solar.
Nuclear power is the only method used to generate electricity in the UK.

questions.question: In many active thermal power stations across the UK, how is water converted into steam to begin the process of electricity generation?
options: By using solar panels to focus sunlight directly onto the water pipes.
By burning natural gas and oil to heat the water.
By mixing water with highly reactive alkali metals to cause an exothermic reaction.
By passing the water through volcanic geothermal vents.

questions.question: In a thermal power station, what is the correct sequence of physical actions that leads to the generation of electricity?
options: Moving steam pushes turbines, which drive electric generators that produce electricity.
Burning fuel directly spins the electric generators without needing a turbine.
Steam cools down into liquid water, which directly powers the electric outlets.
Electric generators boil the water, which then pushes the turbines backwards.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the use of fossil fuels in UK power stations today?
options: Coal is the primary fossil fuel burned, while natural gas has been completely phased out.
Natural gas and oil are fossil fuels used in power stations, whereas coal is no longer used.
Both coal and wood have been entirely banned, leaving oil as the sole energy source.
Fossil fuels are no longer used in any capacity in UK power stations.

questions.question: When evaluating different combustible fuels, which group of fuels all release greenhouse gases and pollutants when they are burned?
options: Natural gas, oil, waste, and wood
Wind, solar, falling water, and geothermal
Hydrogen, oxygen, and pure liquid nitrogen
Only coal and crude oil, while wood and waste burn completely cleanly

questions.question: Why are wind, solar, and hydroelectric energy classified as renewable resources?
options: They can be burned multiple times without losing any of their mass.
They will not run out because they are replenished more quickly than we use them up.
They do not transfer any energy to the surroundings when they are used.
They are created artificially in laboratories at a very low cost.
